newsitem.title: USA: Sun-Diamond trial concludes; verdict likely Friday.
newsitem.headline: Sun-Diamond trial concludes; verdict likely Friday.

text.p: The trial of fruit cooperative Sun-Diamond Growers of California concluded on Wednesday, and a verdict was expected by the end of the week on whether the giant concern broke federal laws by giving gifts and favors to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.
The outcome of the trial could have significant ramifications in other pending cases in the government's widespread two-year investigation of the former Clinton cabinet member, legal experts say.

A conviction of any or all of the nine criminal counts Sun-Diamond is charged with could persuade reluctant witnesses to cooperate in other indictments, while a loss could take the wind out of the government's sails, legal sources believe.
The Sun-Diamond trial is the first case to come to court as the result of the government's probe of Espy led by independent counsel Donald Smaltz.

So far the investigation has resulted in five sets of criminal indictments and charges being brought against more than a dozen individuals and concerns, including the Washington lobbyist for the huge Arkansas-based chicken processor Tyson Foods, and observers have said the indictments are drawing a tighter circle around the former cabinet secretary.
Espy resigned as head of the huge federal agency in 1994 amid a swirl of accusations that he had taken illegal gifts and favors from companies his agency was charged to regulate.

The government has charged Sun-Diamond Growers with a calculated pattern of plying Espy with expensive dinners and outings -- including favors to his girlfriend and illegal campaign contributions to his brother -- because of his senior position in the administration. Sun-Diamond has denied all charges.
The court will not be session on Thursday, and a verdict is expected when jurors reconvene on Friday.
